newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says January sales surged 18.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: VW says January sales surged 18.1 percent.

text.p: Volkswagen AG, helped by strong performances in Brazil and Asia, said Thursday that sales last month surged 18 percent to 329,300 vehicles despite a sluggish market at home.
VW said passenger car sales under the VW brand rose 15 percent to 212,500, while its Audi luxury brand rose 32 percent to 43,800.
In North America, VW's sales rose 21 percent to 16,000 vehicles, while sales rose 60 percent to 22,600 vehicles in China, where the carmaker is the No. 1 selling brand.

VW's sales in Brazil, a key market where the carmaker has production facilities, surged 45 percent to 57,400 vehicles, while sales in Japan rose 36 percent to 4,000 vehicles following heavy advertising and marketing.
The Wolfsburg-based carmaker said January sales in Germany, however, edged up only 2 percent to 73,300 vehicles from 71,870 in January 1996.
It added that sales at its Czech Skoda unit rose 7.5 percent to 18,100 and they rose 18 percent to 28,500 at Spanish-based SEAT.
Volkswagen said all of its brands contributed to the higher sales, which it said were driven by new vehicles that were launched in late 1996 and were finally reaching major markets.
VW late last year launched a number of new vehicles, including a remodeled VW Passat and the new Audi A3, a three-door model that has become the new entry point at VW's luxury car division.
"The sales increase in January is clearly the result of our product offensive and the roll-out of new vehicles," a VW spokesman said.
